findings.fix: Move this value to a .env file (and ensure .env is in .gitignore). Rotate the compromised credential.

findings.title: Math.random() used for security-sensitive value
findings.description: Math.random() is not cryptographically secure and is being used near authentication, token, password, OTP, session, or CSRF context.
findings.why: Math.random() is a predictable pseudo-random generator seeded from clock/context. An attacker who sees a few outputs can predict the next one — fine for animation, catastrophic for tokens or OTPs.
findings.fix: Use crypto.randomBytes() or crypto.getRandomValues() instead.

findings.title: Use of eval()
findings.description: eval() executes arbitrary code and is a security risk.
findings.why: eval() turns any user-controlled string into executable code. If any input reaches it, remote code execution is one line away.
findings.fix: Remove eval() and use safer alternatives.

findings.title: XSS (innerHTML)
findings.description: innerHTML is assigned from user-controlled input, which can lead to XSS.
findings.why: innerHTML parses its input as HTML — scripts, event handlers, iframes. If any user-controlled string reaches it unsanitized, XSS follows.
findings.fix: Use textContent for plain text, or sanitize trusted HTML with DOMPurify.

findings.title: Stack trace / error message leaked in HTTP response
findings.description: An error's stack or message is being sent back to the client. Stack traces disclose file paths, package versions, and internal function names; error messages often include ids and database internals.
findings.why: res.send(err.stack) is the debuggable version of a catch handler. It's how you make a demo feel responsive. In production it hands attackers your directory layout, dependency versions, database schema, and — often — the actual query that failed. Every internal-scan-turns-into-a-CVE story includes one of these lines.
findings.fix: Log the error server-side (pino/winston/sentry). Return a generic message: `res.status(500).json({ error: 'Internal server error' })`.

findings.title: IDOR — record looked up by user-supplied id without ownership check
findings.description: A route reads an id from the request and queries the database by that id, with no ownership predicate in the handler body. Any authenticated user can pass another user's id.
findings.why: Models can infer 'who are you' (auth is well-documented in tutorials) but not 'may you' (authorization depends on the app's data model). The result is the classic IDOR: /api/invoice/1234 → /api/invoice/1235 returns someone else's record. Every one of these is the same shape.
findings.fix: Add an ownership predicate to the query: `where: { id, userId: req.user.id }`. Never trust that authentication alone implies authorization.

findings.fix: Restrict CORS to specific trusted origins instead of *.

findings.title: Math.random() used for security-sensitive value
findings.description: Math.random() is not cryptographically secure and is being used near authentication, token, password, OTP, session, or CSRF context.
findings.why: Math.random() is a predictable pseudo-random generator seeded from clock/context. An attacker who sees a few outputs can predict the next one — fine for animation, catastrophic for tokens or OTPs.
findings.fix: Use crypto.randomBytes() or crypto.getRandomValues() instead.

findings.description: An error's stack or message is being sent back to the client. Stack traces disclose file paths, package versions, and internal function names; error messages often include ids and database internals.

findings.title: IDOR — record looked up by user-supplied id without ownership check
findings.description: A route reads an id from the request and queries the database by that id, with no ownership predicate in the handler body. Any authenticated user can pass another user's id.
findings.why: Models can infer 'who are you' (auth is well-documented in tutorials) but not 'may you' (authorization depends on the app's data model). The result is the classic IDOR: /api/invoice/1234 → /api/invoice/1235 returns someone else's record. Every one of these is the same shape.
findings.fix: Add an ownership predicate to the query: `where: { id, userId: req.user.id }`. Never trust that authentication alone implies authorization.

findings.title: Vendored library with known CVE: jquery@1.11.2.min
findings.description: XSS in jQuery as used in Drupal, Backdrop CMS, and other products
findings.why: This library is checked into the repo (not managed by npm), so it never appears in your lockfile and `npm audit` won't see it. But the file IS served to every browser that loads your app. If the CVE is exploitable, every visitor is exposed. Rotate to a patched version or remove.
findings.fix: Update the vendored copy of `jquery` to the patched version, or delete the file and install via npm so `npm audit` catches future issues.
